name: Bath vs shower

summary: The Bath vs shower calculator works out weekly shower frequency (Shower preferences) from the shower flow rate, the average shower duration, the shower frequency and the total water used for shower. That makes it useful for a practical question that turns up in daily life. Editing anything puts the results away until the next press of Calculate — change one value at a time and the updated answer tells you what that value was worth.

sections.title: How does the Bath vs shower calculator work?
sections.html:
The Bath vs shower calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports weekly shower frequency (Shower preferences) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the showering style, the initial shower power and the shower power while lathering); then you type in the shower flow rate, the average shower duration, the shower frequency and the total water used for shower (Shower preferences).

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

11 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Bath vs shower calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Weekly shower frequency=(-shower frequency + daily shower frequency × compare my water usage on a...) ÷ (compare my water usage on a... − 1)
Weekly shower frequency=(-shower frequency (staggered) + daily shower frequency × compare my water usage on a...) ÷ (compare my water usage on a... − 1)
Shower power=total water used for shower ÷ (average shower duration × shower flow rate × shower frequency)
Total duration the shower is turned on=average shower duration × shower frequency
Shower power when rinsing=(-shower flow rate × shower frequency (staggered) × (↳ Initial shower duration × initial shower power + ↳ Lathering duration × shower power while lathering) + total water used for shower) ÷ (shower flow rate × shower frequency (staggered) × ↳ Rinsing shower duration)
Shower duration=shower frequency (staggered) × (↳ Initial shower duration + ↳ Lathering duration + ↳ Rinsing shower duration)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Shower flow rate: Flow rate, opening in liters per minute
  • Average shower duration: Time, opening in minutes
  • Shower frequency: Time, opening in days
  • Daily shower frequency (Shower preferences): Time, opening in days
  • Weekly shower frequency (Shower preferences): Time, opening in weeks
  • Total water used for shower (Shower preferences): Volume, opening in liters
  • ↳ Initial shower duration: Time, opening in minutes
  • ↳ Lathering duration: Time, opening in minutes

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Bath vs shower calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the shower flow rate, the average shower duration and the shower frequency — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Bath vs shower calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns weekly shower frequency (Shower preferences), derived from the shower flow rate, the average shower duration and the shower frequency. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Bath vs shower calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the shower flow rate, the average shower duration, the shower frequency and the total water used for shower, which is 25 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter shower flow rate in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Shower flow rate opens in liters per minute and the chip beside it offers 39 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (11 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Shower frequency = 168 days. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Bath vs shower calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
